**Credit card (Reg Z, 1026.12(b)):** Cardholder liability for unauthorized use cannot exceed the lesser of $50 or the value of what the thief obtained before the issuer was notified [R-1026.12#1]. Unauthorized transfers shown on a periodic statement must be reported within 60 days of the statement's transmittal to avoid liability for later transfers [R-1005.6#1]. A lower liability under state law or agreement also controls [R-1005.6#2].

**Short answer:** The evidence gives the Regulation E debit-card liability limits and the Regulation Z billing-error deadlines. It does not include the Regulation Z credit card liability cap (§1026.12(b)), so I can't state that limit.

**Debit/checking (Reg E)**
- A consumer can be held liable only if the institution gave the required disclosures. If an access device was involved, it must be an accepted device and the institution must have provided a means to identify the consumer [R-1005.6#1].
- Liability is capped at the lesser of $50 or the unauthorized transfers made before notice if the consumer notifies within two business days after learning of the loss or theft [R-1005.6#1].
- If the consumer misses that window, liability is capped at the lesser of $500 or the sum of the amounts described in §1005.6(b)(2) [R-1005.6#1].
- The consumer must report an unauthorized transfer shown on a periodic statement within 60 days of the statement's transmittal to avoid liability for later transfers [R-1005.6#1].
- Delay caused by extenuating circumstances extends these times to a reasonable period. A lower state-law or agreement limit controls [R-1005.6#1][R-1005.6#2].
- Error notice is timely if received within 60 days after the statement showing the error is sent. The institution may require written confirmation within 10 business days of an oral notice [R-1005.11#1].
- The institution must determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days. If it cannot, it may take up to 45 days, provided it meets the further conditions in §1005.11(c)(2), which the excerpt cuts off [R-1005.11#1].

**Credit card (Reg Z)**
- An extension of credit to someone without actual, implied, or apparent authority is a billing error [R-1026.13#1].
- The written notice must reach the creditor within 60 days after the first statement showing the error [R-1026.13#1].
- The creditor must acknowledge within 30 days and resolve within two billing cycles, and no later than 90 days [R-1026.13#1].
- While the error is pending, the consumer need not pay the disputed amount, and adverse credit reporting on it is prohibited [R-1026.13#2].
- For cases involving both credit and electronic fund transfers, §1026.12(g) points to Regulation E §1005.12(a) on liability for unauthorized use [R-1026.12#3].

**Our data:** Our CFPB sample shows 196 complaints with the keyword "unauthorized" from 2026-04-01 to 2026-07-29 [S-1]. It is not split by product or card type and does not represent the whole market.
